info.name: lumen — dev API (§1 public · §8 admin · §9 bao)
info.description:
Local dev against `make dev` (server on :8080, seeded corpus).

Fastest path: variables pre-filled with the dev placeholders (gofar / mellon-dev-password). Run a login request first — it captures {{token}} into the collection; every admin request inherits it (collection-level Bearer auth).

Folders are SELF-CLEANING and rerunnable: demo post soft-deleted, uploaded photo deleted, vocabulary rows persist by design (201-or-409), bao path version-bumps.

§9 folder needs the plane bootstrapped: `make dev-plane` then restart `make dev` (it auto-loads dev-plane.env). Without it the routes honestly do not exist (404).

request.description: liveness: process answers.
readiness: Postgres AND the engine must answer (fixture mode 503s honestly).

item.name: posts — curation order, absent limit = corpus

request.description: total reflects ALL published; items in rank order (engine-owned, deterministic).
offset/limit; total still the FULL filtered count.
repeated tag= is OR-matched (§1).
sort=newest|oldest|quickest|longest; unknown sort is a 400, never silent curation.
THE leak rule: the draft IS in the index (admin door needs it) — hydration + status filter keep it out. This 404 is the doctrine.
ranking is Meilisearch's; assertions are rules (found, sane), not exact order.
8 seeded gallery photos; the featured hero is NOT gallery — total proves it.
curation point read from truth.
counts are publish-maintained (§1), never aggregated at read.

item.name: Admin §8 — posts lifecycle

request.description: credentials = argon2id row (cmd/userctl); unknown user and wrong password answer ONE indistinguishable 401. Run this FIRST for every admin folder.

exec: pm.test("expiresIn is the server-decided 12h (mellon AdminApi camelCase)", () => pm.expect(j.expiresIn).to.eql(12*60*60));

item.name: admin list — drafts ARE visible here

request.description: the mirror of the leak rule: admin sees everything, envelope {total,items,page,pageSize 20}.

exec: pm.test("fresh draft: status draft, rev 1", () => { pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("draft"); pm.expect(j.rev).to.eql(1); });

request.description: live-namespace unique index rejects.
optimistic lock: mismatched rev touches NOTHING (RowsAffected-verified — closes the TOCTOU too).

item.name: update with current rev → rev bumps

request.description: one tx: derivations (preview default = first paragraph, word_count/read_time from FINAL content, rank assign, content_hash) + state machine + the river index job committed INSIDE via InsertTx.

exec: pm.test("publish derivations land", () => { pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("published"); pm.expect(j.readTime).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(j.preview).to.include("First paragraph"); pm.expect(j.publishedAt).to.not.eql(null); });

request.description: content_hash idempotence: byte-identical input must not re-rank — deterministic caches depend on it.
the palette's finder: engine WITHOUT the status clause; three groups ≤8 (posts/photos/tags). Draft surfacing HERE and nowhere public is the tested feature.
machine: draft→published⇄unpublished. Shipped posts never return to draft.
row hidden, media GC-windowed; the worker reads truth→ finds the row gone→ deletes the DOC. Convergence as access control.

item.name: RE-create same slug → 201 (delete FREED the slug)

request.description: partial unique (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) — history keeps its row, the slug returns to the live namespace.

item.description: Run folder-order top-to-bottom; it self-cleans (deleted_at rows persist for the GC window by design).

request.description: collection= accepts repeated values; gallery=1|0; from/to on created_at. NOTE: later requests act on {{photoId}} which ONLY the upload captures — the folder is safe to rerun and never touches seeded rows.

lumen DECODES (client type-claims are suggestions), REBUILDS (EXIF dies by construction), PUTs S3, commits row+GC-ledger+index job in one tx. Fresh photos: gallery=false, collection=null — surfacing is a deliberate act. In Postman, RE-SELECT postman/sample.png in the Body→file field (paths are machine-local).

item.name: references of the uploaded photo (delete warn-list)

request.description: content scan: which posts embed this src — warn with full information, never block. Runs AFTER upload ({{photoId}} is upload-owned).
alt arrives filename-derived ("sample") — the author edits it; truth stays human.

item.name: delete (row gone; object outlives until storage GC)

request.description: eager creation: the vocabulary exists the moment it is declared, used or not. 409 on reruns is EXPECTED (rows persist — 201/409 both prove the rule).
revocation itself: every outstanding JWT carries the old tv → all dead, instantly, across replicas. No session cache to invalidate.
THE proof the JWT+tv design exists for. {{token}} still holds it — signature valid, truth says no.

exec: pm.test("the revoked token is dead", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(401));
pm.test("expiresIn is the server-decided 12h (mellon AdminApi camelCase)", () => pm.expect(j.expiresIn).to.eql(12*60*60));

paths (names only — never bytes on a list)

request.description: lumen LOGS never see these bytes: the battery asserts op lines exist and values do not.

item.name: CAS write with cas=0 on an EXISTING path → 409

request.description: stale cas → conflict, NEVER a silent clobber. The mount itself is cas_required — unconditional puts are refused at the plane too.

item.name: CAS write with fresh cas → new version

request.description: {{casNow}} captured by the metadata request — if you run this alone it 409s (correctly): run the folder in order.
